$comment: Areas of effect (SPEC §17.1, §33.4), hand-verified against the SRD 5.2.1 PDF. `page` is where the quoted text is printed (the build checks the spell is on that page); `source` quotes or paraphrases the PDF and explains any mapping. Flat shapes (a square or circle on the ground) have no §17.1 equivalent, so they map to the Cube / Sphere with the same footprint; `area: null` marks a size limit (an object or illusion), not an area of effect. Walls: `length × height × thickness` in feet, `ring` = diameter of the ring/globe form, `opaque` blocks sight, `blocksMove` = solid barrier.

alarm.source: "Choose a door, a window, or an area within range that is no larger than a 20-foot Cube." The warded area is the spell's area (Foundry agrees).

detect-evil-and-good.source: "you sense the location of any Aberration, Celestial, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, or Undead within 30 feet of yourself" — a 30-ft Emanation that moves with you.

detect-magic.source: "you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself" — a 30-ft Emanation that moves with you.

detect-poison-and-disease.source: "you sense the location of poisons, poisonous or venomous creatures, and magical contagions within 30 feet of yourself".

detect-thoughts.source: Sense Thoughts: "You sense the presence of thoughts within 30 feet of yourself"; Read Thoughts targets one creature within 30 feet.

druidcraft.source: "The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube" is a size limit for a harmless sensory effect, not an area of effect (Foundry's cube template not used).

ice-knife.source: "Make a ranged spell attack against the target … Hit or miss, the shard then explodes. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 Cold damage." The explosion is centred on the target, not on the caster, so it is not an Emanation template; the DM adds the creatures within 5 feet on the resolution card.
ice-knife.review: No area template: the 5-ft explosion is centred on the attack's target; the DM adds nearby creatures on the card.

phantasmal-force.source: "a phantasmal object, creature, or other phenomenon that is no larger than a 10-foot Cube" — a size limit on the phantasm, not an area.

creation.source: "The object must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube" (+5 ft per slot) — object size, not an area.

passwall.source: A passage (5 ft wide, 8 ft tall, 20 ft deep) through a surface — a created opening, not an area of effect.

planar-ally.source: Summons an entity's servant; Foundry's 5-ft circle is only a token footprint, not an area of effect.

programmed-illusion.source: "It must be no larger than a 30-foot Cube" — size limit of the illusion, not an area.

heroes-feast.source: "You conjure a feast that appears on a surface in an unoccupied 10-foot Cube next to you" — where the food appears; creatures benefit by partaking, not by being in an area.

magnificent-mansion.source: Creates a door (5 ft wide, 10 ft tall) to an extradimensional dwelling — a portal, not an area of effect.

demiplane.source: Creates a shadowy door to a demiplane — a portal, not an area of effect.

gate.source: Opens a portal (5 to 20 feet in diameter) to another plane — a portal, not an area of effect.

teleportation-circle.source: "you draw a 5-foot-radius circle on the ground"; creatures that enter the portal are teleported. Flat circle → Sphere of the same radius.
teleportation-circle.review: Flat 5-ft-radius circle on the ground represented as a Sphere of the same radius.

hallow.source: "You touch a point and infuse an area around it … The area can have a radius up to 60 feet" — centred on the touched point and stationary, so a Sphere (not an Emanation from the caster).

guards-and-wards.source: "protects up to 2,500 square feet of floor space. The warded area can be up to 20 feet tall, and you shape it as one 50-foot square" (or smaller contiguous squares). Footprint as a 50-ft Cube; the 20-ft height limit stays in the text.
guards-and-wards.review: 50-ft square footprint as a 50-ft Cube; the warded area is at most 20 ft tall and may be split into smaller squares.

forcecage.source: "A prison in the shape of a cage can be up to 20 feet on a side … A prison in the shape of a box can be up to 10 feet on a side".

areaAlternatives.label: Solid box (up to 10 feet on a side)

earthquake.source: "an intense tremor rips through the ground in a 100-foot-radius circle centered on that point"; only creatures on the ground are affected. Flat circle → Sphere of the same radius (the DM removes flying creatures).
earthquake.review: Flat 100-ft-radius circle represented as a Sphere; only creatures on the ground are affected (DM removes flyers).

storm-of-vengeance.source: "A churning storm cloud forms … centered on a point within range and spreading to a radius of 300 feet. Each creature under the cloud …" Radius 300 as a Sphere (creatures under the cloud).
storm-of-vengeance.review: Cloud of radius 300 ft represented as a Sphere centred on the point; the text affects creatures under the cloud.

fire-storm.source: "The area of the storm consists of up to ten 10-foot Cubes, which you arrange as you like. Each Cube must be contiguous with at least one other Cube." One 10-ft Cube per placement; up to ten.
fire-storm.review: One 10-ft Cube template per placement; the caster may place up to ten contiguous Cubes.

flaming-sphere.source: "You create a 5-foot-diameter sphere of fire … Any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the sphere makes a Dexterity saving throw". The damaging zone is a 5-ft Emanation from the sphere object (§17.1: distance + the source's radius), which moves when you move the sphere.
flaming-sphere.review: The damaging zone is a 5-ft Emanation from the sphere as an object token (5-ft diameter).

call-lightning.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "It takes the shape of a Cylinder that is 10 feet tall with a 60-foot radius." (the storm cloud; each bolt hits creatures within 5 feet of a chosen point).

conjure-celestial.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "a pillar of light in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder".

flame-strike.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "Each creature in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder".

ice-storm.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "Hail falls in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder".

magic-circle.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "You create a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-tall Cylinder of magical energy".

moonbeam.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "A silvery beam of pale light shines down in a 5-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder".

reverse-gravity.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "This spell reverses gravity in a 50-foot-radius, 100-foot high Cylinder". The height is split across a line break in the PDF ("100-" / "foot").

sleet-storm.source: SPEC §33.4 cylinder: "sleet falls in a 40-foot-tall, 20-foot-radius Cylinder".

antilife-shell.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "An aura extends from you in a 10-foot Emanation for the duration." Moves with you.

antimagic-field.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "An aura of antimagic surrounds you in 10-foot Emanation." Moves with you.

conjure-woodland-beings.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "nature spirits that flit around you in a 10-foot Emanation for the duration".

globe-of-invulnerability.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "An immobile, shimmering barrier appears in a 10-foot Emanation around you". The distance is split across a line break in the PDF ("10-" / "foot"); immobile.

tiny-hut.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "A 10-foot Emanation springs into existence around you and remains stationary for the duration."

conjure-minor-elementals.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "spirits … that flit around you in a 15-foot Emanation for the duration".

spirit-guardians.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "Protective spirits flit around you in a 15-foot Emanation for the duration."

aura-of-life.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "An aura radiates from you in a 30-foot Emanation for the duration."

holy-aura.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "For the duration, you emit an aura in a 30-foot Emanation."

pass-without-trace.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "You radiate a concealing aura in a 30-foot Emanation for the duration."

speak-with-plants.source: SPEC §33.4 emanation: "You imbue plants in an immobile 30-foot Emanation".

darkness.source: "magical Darkness spreads from a point within range and fills a 15-foot-radius Sphere … Alternatively, you cast the spell on an object … causing the Darkness to fill a 15-foot Emanation originating from that object" (moves with the object).

areaAlternatives.label: Cast on an object: 15-foot Emanation that moves with the object

daylight.source: "sunlight spreads from a point within range and fills a 60-foot-radius Sphere … Alternatively, you cast the spell on an object … causing the sunlight to fill a 60-foot Emanation originating from that object" (moves with the object).

areaAlternatives.label: Cast on an object: 60-foot Emanation that moves with the object

wall-of-fire.source: "You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque … One side of the wall, selected by you when you cast this spell, deals 5d8 Fire damage … The other side of the wall deals no damage." Creatures can pass through (not a barrier). damagingSide: one side, chosen at casting (`left` of the drawn line; the caster flips it when placing).
wall-of-fire.review: damagingSide defaults to the left of the drawn line; the caster picks the side when casting.

wall-of-force.source: "An Invisible wall of force … You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a globe with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels … the wall is 1/4 inch thick … Nothing can physically pass through the wall." Ten panels in a row: 100 × 10 ft; thickness 1/48 ft; globe = 20-ft ring; invisible, so not opaque.
wall-of-force.review: Ten 10×10 panels represented as one straight 100 × 10 ft wall (the panels can be arranged freely).

wall-of-ice.source: "You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a globe with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-square panels … the wall is 1 foot thick … The wall is an object that can be damaged and thus breached." A solid barrier; the PDF does not say whether it blocks sight (left transparent).
wall-of-ice.review: Opacity isn't stated in the SRD (left transparent); ten panels represented as one straight 100 × 10 ft wall.

wall-of-stone.source: "A nonmagical wall of solid stone … The wall is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels … Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick." Solid stone: opaque and a barrier.
wall-of-stone.review: Ten panels represented as one straight wall; the 10-by-20-ft panel alternative's orientation is the caster's choice.

areaAlternatives.label: Ten 10-by-20-foot panels, 3 inches thick (oriented as you choose)

wall-of-thorns.source: "You choose to make the wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick or a circle that has a 20-foot diameter and is up to 20 feet high and 5 feet thick. The wall blocks line of sight." Creatures can move through it (4 feet of movement per foot).

wind-wall.source: "You can make the wall up to 50 feet long, 15 feet high, and 1 foot thick … so long as it makes one continuous path along the ground." Only Small or smaller flyers, gases and ordinary projectiles are stopped, so it is not a barrier to creatures; not opaque.

blade-barrier.source: "You make a straight wall up to 100 feet long, 20 feet high, and 5 feet thick, or a ringed wall up to 60 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 5 feet thick. The wall provides Three-Quarters Cover, and its space is Difficult Terrain." Passable, not opaque.

prismatic-wall.source: "a vertical opaque wall—up to 90 feet long, 30 feet high, and 1 inch thick … Alternatively, you shape the wall into a globe up to 30 feet in diameter". Creatures can pass through (layer by layer), so it is not a movement barrier; thickness 1/12 ft.

tsunami.source: "A wall of water springs into existence … You can make the wall up to 300 feet long, 300 feet high, and 50 feet thick." Creatures are carried inside it; opacity not stated.
tsunami.review: Opacity of the wall of water isn't stated in the SRD (left transparent).
